The proof contract for ws7 does not name the skill-wiring check as a discrete acceptance criterion, only the file-system operations.

The manifest carryover from Phase 1 is explicitly flagged as incomplete: 'memory-state-substrate-contracts.manifest.json still points 4x schema_or_parser + fixture_roots[0] at the old .agent/state/collaboration/ homes — repoint (verify gate-loaded vs descriptive first).' This is a load-bearing cross-reference in a schema-resolution chain that spans three distinct mechanisms (live-types.ts constants, collaboration-json-validation.ts self-deriving path, compile-time JSON imports). A stale manifest under an active gate-loaded path is a silent schema-location split — the validator may load the wrong (old) schema path while the manifest claims correctness.

Three schema-resolution mechanisms are acknowledged to have been in tension (line 275-284): live-types.ts PATH constants, collaboration-json-validation.ts self-deriving schema dir from data file path, and compile-time JSON imports plus test fixtures. The corrected decouple (repo-root-relative to agent-tools/src/collaboration-state/schemas/) resolves the tsc/dist dead-path problem, but the plan records this as 'Phase-1 work is landed' without a first-hand post-landing gate verification being cited in the accepted proof. The characterisation harness (agent-tools suite) is named as the green-before/after guard, but the acceptance criterion for ws7 (line 354) does not explicitly require a gate-green signal for this specific schema decouple.

The repo/instance content-boundary architecture introduced in WS7 (repo tier = versioned/shared vs instance tier = one checkout's live state) is a significant structural reclassification. The plan correctly names the untrack as relying on a 'mandatory standing curation obligation' (lines 309-310), but the architectural enforcement surface for that obligation is exclusively social/doctrinal (skill-wiring). There is no structural gate that prevents an agent from operating on instance-tier comms knowledge without first curating it — the safety net is procedural, not mechanical, which is a known fragility class for a standing obligation.

The untrack boundary decision (lines 327-331) includes 'conversations/' and 'escalations/' and lean 'sidebars/' as tracked, while 'comms/' + 'comms-seen/' + claims + shared-comms-log + comms-archive + comms-draft + handoffs go untracked (preserve-on-disk). This boundary is owner-delegated but the plan does not record the architectural rationale for why conversations/escalations/sidebars earn tracked status while handoffs do not — handoffs carry succession-critical continuity state and their untracking is architecturally significant.

The WS2 survey commands (lines 174-185) use one node process per file over ~5,000 files ('slow but dependency-free') and acknowledge batching as an agent option into /tmp. The plan names /tmp as the batch scratch target, which is the repo-conventional scratchpad for analysis, but the no-unbounded-host-load rule applies; no cap or chunk-size guard is named in the survey command block.

The 'ArcAngel relocation — owner-directed early WS7 slice' log entry (lines 189-203) states the ArcAngel channel was relocated via 'git mv' to .agent/collaboration/rapid-comms/ but also notes that .agent/collaboration/ is 'the chosen tracked home (parallel to the untracked-bound .agent/state/collaboration/)' with 'WS7/owner may refine the path.' The plan does not mark this path as frozen or require a prior-to-move coordination window.

The finding-provenance discipline (blind-arisen / seeded-confirmed / statistically-derived / cross-attested, lines 138-141) is architecturally sound for a research corpus where contamination is a declared risk. The four-category taxonomy cleanly separates epistemic source from content, which is the correct decouple for a trust-but-verify synthesis.

The plan correctly applies the repo-root-relative schema path resolution strategy (lines 281-283) to solve the tsc dist path dead-path problem, which is the correct architectural choice: tsx (source-run) and the built CLI both resolve from repo root, whereas module-relative paths diverge between the two runtimes. specialist_findings.claim: Phase 2.2 records two contradictory shim shapes. The acceptance code block at line 504 shows the shim importing from 'agent-tools/dist/artefacts/verify.js', but the CI build-ordering decision at line 510 resolves to Option B: importing from 'agent-tools/src/' via tsx, not dist/. The acceptance block is never corrected to match the decided shape. A reader grounding the shim against the plan sees one shape in prose and the opposite in the code block, which is a maintenance-time confusion risk and a spec-vs-implementation divergence.

The skills-lock.json concurrency mitigation is split across two places with different strategies. Section 4.1 (line 633) says 'start with optimistic-concurrency check on version' (read-modify-write with a version field). The risk register (line 887) says 'advisory lock file (e.g. skills-lock.json.lock) acquired before read-modify-write'. These are not the same mechanism: optimistic concurrency detects collisions after the fact; advisory locking prevents concurrent entry. The plan does not reconcile which strategy Phase 4.1 actually implements, leaving the architect of that cycle with an ambiguous contract.

The skill-load budget default (Phase 6.1, line 706) is deferred to execution time via 'claude /doctor', with the value computed as reported-maximum × 0.85. This is correct in principle, but the CLI's verify command must also enforce this threshold in CI where 'claude /doctor' is not available. The plan does not specify how the threshold value is persisted after Phase 6.1 measurement — no config file, no package.json field, no env-var name — so the CI enforcement path is unarchitected. If the value is baked into a config file at measurement time, that mechanism needs to be named; if it is re-measured on each CI run, that is a runtime dependency on claude CLI in CI which conflicts with the headless nature of a lint gate.

Phase 3.5 (add-hook, line 602) references hooks-portability.plan.md as an adjacent plan that hook content 'derives from', and the Predecessor/Successor section (line 937) says 'reconcile during Phase 3 design'. This reconciliation is not a plan todo item — it is informal prose. If hooks-portability.plan.md has already made architectural decisions about the Layer-1 hook policy entry format, Phase 3.5 implementation may silently diverge from it. A cross-plan reconciliation gate (even a single acceptance criterion) is missing.

Phase 5.2 (description form check, line 673) introduces a 'heuristic match plus an allow-list' for skills that 'already convey when implicitly'. The allow-list is documented in test fixtures, not in a canonical config location accessible to the CLI at runtime. If the allow-list grows or needs auditing, there is no single CLI-surfaced source of truth — the plan does not specify whether the allow-list is embedded in verify.ts, in a JSON sidecar, or derivable from a flag. This is a minor extensibility gap but creates a maintenance surface outside the CLI contract.

The plan correctly identifies that '.claude/settings.json enabled-plugin list is read by plugin-audit but never mutated by the CLI' (line 336). This is sound — settings remain owner-controlled. The architecture also correctly places the single canonical location as '.agent/' with adapters as generated-only. These invariants at lines 311-321 are well-formed and directly enforce the PDR-009 three-layer model.

The linear dependency chain from Phase 3.0 through 7.1 (todos id 3-0 through 7-1) means every phase from 3 onwards blocks on all preceding phases completing. The plan correctly pulled shared helpers into a 3.0 precondition cycle to enable parallel landing of 3.1-3.5. However, Phases 5 and 6 depend on 2-3-strict-spec-flag (line 86, 101) but spec compliance and budget checks are logically independent of the adapter-generation work in Phase 3-4. The strictly linear depends_on chain means Phase 5 cannot start until the full authoring CLI (Phase 3) and update/remove CLI (Phase 4) are complete, which may extend the timeline without providing isolation. This is a scheduling observation, not a correctness defect.
